summary: Cross-org API key rotation led to misattributed usage and incorrect credit application
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after rotating multiple API keys across subaccounts, usage for some requests was billed to the parent org and not the originating subaccount. This resulted in incorrect invoice line items and auto-applied credits to the wrong billing entity.

Impact:
- VeraHealth saw ~18k token usage attributed to parent org over a 6-hour window on 2026-03-09.
- Invoices and credit memos were generated for the parent account, customer-facing billing dashboard shows different totals than internal metering.
- Customer unable to reconcile month-to-date spend; potential accounting impact for month close.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (dedicated customer pool), prod - us-east-1
- Affected models: redwood-llm-13b (primary), openllama-3b (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Rotate API keys for subaccount A and subaccount B via Console -> API Keys.
2) Reconfigure service to use new keys for microservice behind a load balancer.
3) Make 1000s of inference requests in canary then full traffic.
4) Notice billing dashboard shows a spike on parent billing org while subaccount counters do not reflect corresponding consumption.

Observed behavior:
- Token usage appears on parent org ledger and invoices; subaccount usage counters lag or remain unchanged.
- Credits issued by finance for an unrelated rate correction landed on the parent invoice.

Expected behavior:
- Rotated keys should attribute usage to the issuing subaccount. Credits/adjustments should apply to the same billing entity associated with the usage.

Initial logs/IDs:
- Customer provided request IDs: req_20260309_us_01 -> multiple 5xx and 200 traces observed.
- Billing snapshot times: 2026-03-09T02:00Z - 2026-03-09T08:00Z
- Customer console screenshot attached in ticket (not included here).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - VeraHealth (Priya R.) : We rotated keys at 01:45 UTC and saw the parent invoice reflect the spike. Please help — finance is asking for corrections.
2026-03-10 09:35 - Asha Patel (Support): Thanks Priya — filing an investigation. Can you confirm which subaccount IDs were used, and attach one or two request IDs where the attribution looks wrong?
2026-03-10 10:02 - Priya R. (VeraHealth): Subaccount IDs: sub_acc_4499, sub_acc_4500. Sample request IDs: req_20260309_us_01, req_20260309_us_02. Screenshot of invoice lines attached.

2026-03-11 15:20 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): We've reproduced a case where the key rotation flow resulted in transient mapping to the parent org for keys provisioned via the 'org-level' rotation API. Investigating metering lookup path.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Key rotation endpoint for dedicated customers temporarily creates a parent-scoped key mapping while propagating subaccount mappings to the serving-edge cache.

Query run against metering DB: SELECT sum(tokens) FROM bill_events WHERE timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-09T02:00Z' AND '2026-03-09T08:00Z' AND org_id = 'parent_vera' -> returned ~18,243 tokens; corresponding subaccount events missing for same request_ids.
Edge cache (auth-cache) TTL observed at 5s but propagation lag in dedicated SQS queue was ~7 minutes for rotating keys on that day due to a backlog (see infra PR #1892).

Found fallback behavior: when auth lookup timed out for subaccount mapping, the request auth library fell back to parent-org credential mapping rather than rejecting. This produced misattribution in the metering pipeline.
Correlated with commit https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/4a7d1e which changed fallback in auth library to tolerate missing subaccount mappings (intended to reduce 401s).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-11 18:40 UTC: rolled back tolerant fallback in auth library on dedicated edge (hotfix) and cleared auth-cache entries for impacted keys. Backfill process launched to reassign events: a controlled job will reprocess the affected bill_events for the window 2026-03-09T02:00Z to 2026-03-09T08:00Z and rewrite org_id to correct subaccounts where request_id matches. Finance notified; a temporary credit hold placed on parent invoice to avoid double charges. Follow-ups: (1) postmortem scheduled and linked to INT-4112; (2) add unit/integration tests for key-rotation propagation; (3) increase monitoring around dedicated SQS backlog thresholds. Customer asked for expedited credit memo by 2026-03-15.
